title: LLM Analysis of 150+ years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade

bias_targets.methodology: Using zero-shot and few-shot prompted Large Language Models (LLMs) to annotate expressions of anti-solidarity (defined as opposition, disregard, or exclusion) towards migrants in a historical corpus of German parliamentary debates.
Using LLMs to classify and annotate expressions of anti-solidarity and solidarity towards women in parliamentary speeches, evaluated against thousands of human reference annotations.

Conducting an error analysis by comparing LLM confusion matrices against human annotations to determine if the models exhibit systematic ideological bias (e.g., left-wing bias) by over-predicting anti-solidarity labels.
